value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical cubic girth-six cage and the point-line incidence graph of the Fano plane, whose published locating-domination minimum is six. Counting all 448 optimum detector placements and classifying them into four geometrically inequivalent group orbits is a complete natural finite classification, not a sample or a manufactured numeric slice. The orbit invariant distinguishes collinear/noncollinear triples, selected incidences and point-line imbalance, supplying structural information absent from a bare minimum number. It is potentially useful for choosing symmetric representatives in exact code searches, with no unsupported general theorem claimed.
